sources.title: NetSuite Pricing 2026: Cost Per User, Modules & TCO
NetSuite License Cost 2026: User Seats Explained

keyLimits.en: Third-party estimates put the base platform license around $999-$5,000/month depending on edition and tier, plus $129-$199/month per full user license and $10-$25/month per self-service user; NetSuite publishes no official list price.

addOns.en: Self-service / limited-access user licenses billed separately from full user licenses, per third-party estimates.

cautions.en: NetSuite prices by named user: every person who logs in needs a license, whether used daily or monthly. No public price list exists; each contract is negotiated and bundles a base edition, user licenses and add-on modules. One-time implementation costs can add $25,000 to $750,000 depending on scope, per third-party estimates.

capabilities.en: Cloud ERP suite covering financial management, order management, inventory, procurement and revenue recognition in a single system.

Modular architecture with optional editions (Starter, Mid-Market, Enterprise) and add-on modules such as CRM, e-commerce (SuiteCommerce), and warehouse/inventory management, per third-party pricing research.

limitations.en: No self-serve pricing or sign-up: every deployment requires a sales negotiation and implementation partner, per third-party pricing research.
Per-named-user licensing means costs scale directly with headcount, including occasional/self-service users, per third-party pricing research.

reason.en: Comparable mid-market ERP suite covering finance, inventory and operations for growing companies.
Cloud financial management platform competing for the same mid-market ERP budget.
Microsoft's cloud ERP aimed at the same small-to-mid-market segment as NetSuite.
SAP's cloud ERP for mid-market companies, a direct alternative to NetSuite's positioning.

unknowns: No official published price list; all monetary figures come from third-party pricing research firms, not Oracle/NetSuite directly.
Exact current base license and per-user rates could not be confirmed on an Oracle-owned page within this session's page budget.
